text.title: AI Over-Reliance Self-Audit Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether the period has a measurable substrate at all, then on whether this is a first audit or a repeat, to the one measurement the audit is currently missing.

decision-tree.root-question: For the period under audit, was assistant usage above about an hour a week, and does at least one measurement source exist — repository history, tracker, or agent/session logs?

branch.when: usage under about an hour a week, every diff already peer-reviewed before merge, or no measurement source for the period at all

conclusion.verdict: skip; with no measurable substrate the artefact degrades back to the self-report it exists to replace, and a filled-in pass would license the reliance — emit a structured skip naming which condition held

branch.when: usage is material and at least one measurement source covers the period
branch.question: Is this the first audit period, or does a previous audit exist to trend against?

branch.when: first period; no prior audit and no baseline of any kind
branch.question: Which instrument does the period lack?

branch.when: commits, PRs and tracker data exist, but no timed task was ever performed with completion, chat and agent modes off

conclusion.verdict: run the unassisted drill before scoring — record task, wall-clock time, whether it finished and how many API lookups; without it the audit measures the tool, not the operator

branch.when: the operator has a speedup figure they believe but has never placed next to merge or tracker data

conclusion.verdict: record estimate and measured value side by side with both signs; an item that ends at the estimate records the belief the audit exists to test

branch.when: baseline drill done and both sources available; the period is ready to score

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; score every item against its measurement and emit the artefact with the failed items and their drills

branch.when: a previous audit exists and this period is being compared against it
branch.question: What is weakest in the comparison?

branch.when: throughput was recorded with no stability counterpart — no change-failure rate, revert count, rollback or 24h hotfix count over the same window

conclusion.verdict: pair every throughput item with a stability item over the same window; a throughput-only checklist passes clean while the escape rate climbs

branch.when: the read-before-accept item was scored from memory rather than a random sample of at least 10 AI-attributed hunks

conclusion.verdict: sample the hunks and state control flow and error path from memory before reopening each file; score the share correct, since fluency reads as comprehension

branch.when: code quality was scored by impression; no tool-computed duplication or rewrite-within-two-weeks trend exists

conclusion.verdict: add a trended jscpd or PMD-CPD duplicate-block ratio and the share of added lines rewritten or reverted within two weeks; per-diff judgement structurally cannot see regeneration

branch.when: items failed last period and the remediation recorded was 'be more careful' or 'pay more attention'

conclusion.verdict: convert each failed item into a named drill with a date and a completion check; intent-shaped remediation has no completion state and gets copied forward
